content.value_statement: Database schemas are hard to understand when tables, keys, and indexes are scattered across files. This skill turns schema sources into diagrams, documentation, and relationship analysis.
actual_capabilities: Create Mermaid ERD, PlantUML, dbdiagram.io, Markdown, JSON, and YAML style schema documentation.
Parse SQL dumps, migration files, CREATE TABLE statements, and ORM model examples.
Identify foreign keys, indexes, constraints, cardinality, and many-to-many join tables.
Summarize missing indexes, normalization status, and performance risks.
Compare staging and production schema changes in plain language.
limitations: Does not include executable parser code or a database connector.
Live database analysis requires user-provided access and external tools.
Diagram accuracy depends on complete schema input.
Large databases may need diagrams split by domain.

use_cases.title: Map an Application Schema
use_cases.description: Generate an ERD and relationship notes from migrations or ORM models before changing application data structures.

use_cases.title: Review Database Health
use_cases.description: Find missing indexes, unclear constraints, and normalization issues in a schema review.

use_cases.title: Publish Schema Documentation
use_cases.description: Create readable table documentation and diagrams for onboarding, audits, and technical handoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create an ERD
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid ERD from this database schema. Include tables, primary keys, foreign keys, and relationship labels.

prompt_templates.title: Document Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these table definitions into Markdown documentation. Include columns, constraints, indexes, and short purpose notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review ORM Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these ORM models and explain the relationships, cardinality, missing indexes, and possible performance concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Schema Versions
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these production and staging schemas. Summarize table changes, migration risks, index changes, and documentation updates.

output_examples.input: Prisma models for users, orders, products, and reviews.
output_examples.output: A Mermaid ERD summary, relationship notes, and index recommendations grouped by priority.

output_examples.input: SQL migration files for a new notification feature.
output_examples.output: A schema comparison report showing new tables, changed columns, affected relationships, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: SQLAlchemy models for a multi-tenant project management app.
output_examples.output: Markdown table documentation with constraints, foreign keys, and notes for tenant boundaries.

best_practices: Provide complete schema sources, including migrations, indexes, and constraints.
Ask for a specific output format before generating diagrams or documentation.
Split large schemas by domain so diagrams stay readable.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on partial table lists for relationship analysis.
Do not paste production secrets or live credentials into prompts.
Do not treat generated migration suggestions as tested database changes.

faq.question: Can it generate Mermaid diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on Mermaid ERD output and can also describe PlantUML and dbdiagram.io formats.

faq.question: Can it read ORM models?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for Prisma, TypeORM, SQLAlchemy, Django, and Rails model patterns.

faq.question: Does it connect to my database automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents possible database export tools, but access and execution require user control.

faq.question: Can it find missing indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag common missing indexes on foreign keys, filters, and frequent join columns.

faq.question: Can it compare schema versions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize new tables, changed columns, removed fields, and migration impacts.

faq.question: Is it suitable for large databases?
faq.answer: Yes, but large schemas should be split into domains to keep diagrams clear.
